\chapter{Lo Que --- What, Out of Two Old Words}
\label{ch:lo-que}
\hlchaptermodality{182}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can use lo que for a thing that is never named.}

Complete ES-C53-lo-que: produce lo que digo and contrast it with lo digo.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[lo que]{lo que — \textquotedblleft{}what,\textquotedblright{} out of two old words}

\label{lesson:ES-C53-lo-que}



\begin{quote}
You have \emph{lo}. You have \emph{que}. This chapter puts them next to each other and adds nothing.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: a noun-shaped hole}]
\begin{quote}
\textbf{lo que} — \emph{what}, in the sense of \emph{the thing that}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{\textbf{Lo que} digo} — what I say. \emph{(= the thing that I say)} \emph{\textbf{Lo que} compro} — what I buy.
\end{quote}

Every relative clause so far has hung off a noun: \emph{el libro que compro}. But sometimes there is no noun, because you do not know or do not care what the thing is. \emph{Lo} stands in for it — a placeholder with no gender and nothing behind it — and \emph{que} does its usual job of joining.

So \emph{lo que} is a \textbf{noun-shaped hole with a sentence attached}. That is why it translates as English \emph{what}, which is doing exactly the same thing: \emph{what I say} is \emph{the thing that I say} with the word \emph{thing} taken out.

Now compare it to the \emph{lo} you already know:

\begin{quote}
\emph{Lo digo.} — I say \textbf{it}. \emph{(a specific thing, already named)} \emph{Lo que digo} — \textbf{what} I say. \emph{(no specific thing at all)}
\end{quote}

Same word. In the first it points at something known; in the second it points at a gap the following clause will fill.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}lo digo\textquotedblright{} then \textquotedblleft{}lo que digo\textquotedblright{} — pointing at a thing, then at a gap
  \item \textquotedblleft{}lo que compro\textquotedblright{}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Say \textquotedblleft{}what I buy.\textquotedblright{} (\emph{\textbf{Lo que compro}}.) What is \emph{lo} doing there? (\textbf{Standing in for a thing that is never named.}) How many new words was that? (\textbf{None}.) Next: all of it in one place.
\end{tcolorbox}
